messages:
Sam K: Starting Ceres Labs POC perf run in ~20m. Plan: quick smoke -> 250 qps sustained (20m) -> two short spikes to 1000 qps (2x 3m). SLO asked by prospect: p99 < 200ms for their e-commerce mediations. @Noah M can you confirm Dedicated capacity and any expected overspill behaviors?
Priya V: Confirmed Dedicated pool available (6xA10). Note: sustained 250 qps expected to use ~70% of reserved; spikes will allocate to burst (shared) if not reserved. Ballpark cost delta for spikes: +22% compute for that period.
Sam K: Thanks. We'll run on the 8-bit quantized variant to match customer cost expectations — caveat: quantization sometimes induces a small latency jitter. We'll record both quantized and fp16 runs.
Noah M: Good call. Also FYI: model batching settings default to 8ms coalesce. For their workload (short prompts) we might see higher p50 but lower overall throughput if we change it. Recommend run with default then another with coalesce=16ms.
SalesAssistBot: Sales question: Ceres wants a deterministic fallback path instead of a quality-changing variant if Dedicated is exhausted. Is that possible?
Noah M: We don't offer a transparent queuing guarantee on hosted bursts — we can reserve burst capacity (recommended) or accept fallback to a compatible, smaller model. That will alter outputs; we need their signoff.
Sam K: Understood. We'll keep routing pinned for the baseline run. If fallback occurs we'll capture the timestamps.
DeployBot: Load job scheduled -> job-id: ceres-poc-2350000123-run1.
Sam K: Load command (k6 wrapper):
```
# k6 pseudo
k6 run --vus 250 --duration 20m -e ENDPOINT=https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat -e TOKEN=$POC_KEY script.js
```
Increase VUs for spikes.
[~2h later]
Sam K: Run finished. Baseline (quantized) sustained 250 qps: avg 95ms, p95 150ms, p99 340ms. First spike (1000 qps): avg 410ms, p95 760ms, p99 1.2s. Second spike similar. fp16 baseline was slightly faster: p99 290ms.
Priya V: Those p99s exceed their 200ms ask. Trace shows a surge in batching latency during spikes — queue depth climbed and some requests waited for batch fill. Also saw occasional 8-12% CPU steal on one host during spikes correlated with slower responses.
Sam K: Interesting — quantization increased p99s vs fp16 in baseline. Hypothesis: quantized kernel path has slightly higher variance under batching. Action items: 1) re-run baseline fp16 + coalesce=16ms, 2) run quantized with prefix cache primed, 3) collect per-host histograms and kernel metrics.
Noah M: In simulation, increasing coalesce to 16ms reduced p99 by ~40% at the cost of ~6% extra latency for p50. For them, tail matters more so it's worth proposing. Cost impact minimal.
Priya V: Security note: Ceres asked about KMS envelope encryption and audit log retention 7 years. We provide KMS envelope and can export audit logs to their S3; need to confirm retention policy with legal. Also they required proof of data segregation during POC (no cross-tenant caching) — our infra team validated ephemeral cache per-tenant for this run.
SalesAssistBot: Sales will prepare two quotes: (1) Reserved Dedicated + perf tuning (lower cost), (2) Reserved Dedicated + burst reservation + SLA (higher cost). Also include a non-degradation clause if fallback path is used.
Sam K: I uploaded artifacts: drive/ceres/poc/perf-2350000123-summary.csv and perf-histograms-2350000123.png. CSV columns: phase,qps,avg_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,batching_wait_ms,host_cpu_steal_pct.
Priya V: Next steps: rerun tomorrow with fp16 + coalesce=16ms, then quantized + prefilling prefix cache. Noah, can you run a kernel-level trace on the slower host during the next spike?
Noah M: Will do. Also recommending we offer a short test with burst reservation enabled so Ceres can see deterministic behavior — I'll estimate cost uplift and add to the quote.
Sam K: Thanks. I'll draft the perf digest for the customer outlining tradeoffs (quantized cost vs tail, batching vs p50/p99 tradeoffs) and attach the CSV and histograms. Priya, please attach KMS and audit answers.
Priya V: On it. Flagging EU-data residency preference for certain datasets as a potential enterprise blocker for hosted POC; legal/procurement need to weigh options for Private deployment.
Sam K: Great work team. We'll reconvene after the retest. :rocket:
